findings.description: STRONGEST FINDING. SHEET-MARK-003's text reads as an unconditional rule: keep the prior mark and retry, then 'recording the symbol degraded (no mark) only after it stays non-numeric past the bounded retry window' — i.e. once the window elapses, degrade (no mark) is what happens. All 3 A-direction sketches, working from the text alone, independently implemented exactly that: once the retry bound is exceeded the symbol reports as absent/degraded regardless of whether a prior good price existed — A1's `current_mark()` returns `None` once `degraded=true` even though `last_good` is still `Some`; A2's `published_value` returns `Published::Degraded` (suppressing `cached`) once `RETRY_WINDOW` elapses; A3 goes furthest and explicitly does `self.cached = None` on window elapse. The real code (`read_marks`, sheets-view/src/lib.rs lines ~870-879) does the opposite when a prior mark exists: `Some(PriceReading::Transient) | None => { if let Some(prev) = prior.get(s) { out.marks.insert(s.clone(), *prev); } else { out.degraded.insert(s.clone(), DegradeReason::TimedOut); } }` — a symbol with a prior mark is NEVER recorded degraded no matter how long it stays transient; it just keeps republishing the stale prior `price_cents`/`quote_date` forever (test `transient_keeps_prior_mark_and_retries_degrades_only_after_window`, marks.rs:161-191, drives `max_polls=4`, asserts `client.read_count()==4` yet `produced.degraded.get("AMZN").is_none()`). Degrade-after-window only fires when NO prior mark exists at all (test `no_prior_mark_stays_transient_degrades_after_window`). All 3 B reconstructions pin this exact carry-forward-forever/never-degrade-if-prior-exists rule (B1's 'shall NOT record the symbol as degraded'; B2-c; B3-4). So the spec's literal 'degrade after the window' promise and the code's 'degrade only if there was never a prior mark' behavior are a real, bidirectionally-surfaced contradiction.

The real `PriceReading` enum has THREE states (`Numeric`, `Transient`, `Permanent`), not the two SHEET-MARK-003's text implies ('#N/A'/'Loading...' only). `Permanent` (a terminal, non-retryable error) degrades the symbol immediately with `DegradeReason::Permanent`, discards any prior cached mark (no carry-forward at all, unlike the Transient/TimedOut path), and settles the poll loop without exhausting `max_polls` — pinned by `permanent_error_degrades_immediately_no_prior_carry` (marks.rs:211-241), which asserts both `produced.marks.get("BADX").is_none()` despite a prior mark existing, and `client.read_count() < SettleConfig::default().max_polls`. None of the A-outputs invented this third category — A3 explicitly says 'EARS gives no criterion to distinguish permanent from transient non-numeric,' correctly recognizing the text gives no basis, so this is pure code-side surplus, not an A-side miss. All 3 B outputs reconstruct it in near-identical terms (B1's dedicated 'Unwanted behavior' bullet, B2-f, B3-6) — very stable on the B side.

SECONDARY. 'Bounded retry window' names no mechanism or magnitude. The real code's answer is a POLL-COUNT bound (`SettleConfig.max_polls`, default 8), with the loop breaking exactly at `polls >= cfg.max_polls` — pinned exactly by tests (`max_polls:3` → `read_count()==3`; runtime tests use `max_polls:4` and get exactly 4 reads). This forced the 3 A-outputs to invent divergently: A1 guessed a poll-count bound (`MAX_RETRIES=3`, boundary strictly `>`, i.e. degrade on the 4th bad read) — right kind of mechanism, wrong constant/operator; A2 and A3 both guessed wall-clock `Duration`s (300s and 90s respectively) — the wrong mechanism entirely, since the real bound has no clock in it. The fact that A split 1-count/2-duration (rather than converging) is itself evidence the spec text truly leaves this open, which per the audit's own direction-A semantics ('a sub-decision the spec leaves open, forcing the A-outputs to invent') counts as a legitimate finding, not merely an assumption artifact — and B unanimously supplies the concrete, count-based answer the text omits.

NARROWER. A transport-level failure of the whole `read_price_pass` call (offline/unreachable) is handled as a wholly separate contract from a per-symbol Transient cell reading: `read_marks` propagates the `Err` immediately, produces no `MarksProduced` at all (never a silent empty-but-Ok set — `transport_failure_propagates_error_does_not_emit_empty_marks`, marks.rs:132-159), and explicitly does NOT itself carry `prior` forward — that's pushed to the caller (`runtime`), which retains its own cache across the failed cycle (`runtime/tests/cycle.rs::offline_read_back_propagates_so_caller_retains_prior_marks`). SHEET-MARK-003's text says nothing about this boundary (it only ever discusses a 'Price cell,' not the read call itself failing). B1 and B3 document this in detail with near-identical wording; B2 omits it entirely — a real (if narrow) point of B-instability on this specific sub-item, though it doesn't contradict B1/B3.

MINOR/TANGENTIAL, noted for completeness rather than as a core SHEET-MARK-003 drift. `price_to_cents` degrades non-positive numeric prices (0.0, negative) as `DegradeReason::SubCent` and non-finite prices (NaN, ±Infinity) as `DegradeReason::Permanent` — anomaly handling entirely outside SHEET-MARK-003's text, which addresses only cell-level '#N/A'/'Loading...', not numeric-but-degenerate values. This is very likely governed by a separate EARS ID for the Cents-rounding rule rather than being in scope for the transient-price-cell requirement audited here, so it is not counted among the primary findings.

notes:
Reviewed the real code directly: crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs (PriceReading, DegradeReason, Mark, MarksProduced, SettleConfig, read_marks at lines ~817-887, price_to_cents at ~362), crates/sheets-view/tests/marks.rs (all 10 tests), and crates/runtime/tests/cycle.rs (offline/carry-forward/freshness tests).

A-side stability: unanimous (3/3) on the core, most-consequential structural point — that once the retry bound is exceeded, the mark should report as absent/degraded regardless of a prior good price (A1/A2/A3 all implement this, via `current_mark()`, `published_value`, and explicit `cached=None` respectively). They diverge on the retry-window's exact mechanism/magnitude (A1: poll-count=3, boundary `>`; A2: duration=300s, boundary `>=`; A3: duration=90s, boundary `>`) — a real split, but on a parameter the spec text gives no basis for either way, so I still rate overall aAgreement "high" driven by the structural consensus, while flagging the mechanism split as the source of any instability.

B-side stability: high — all 3 independently and closely reconstruct the settle-loop mechanics, the max_polls poll-count bound, the carry-forward-never-degrade-if-prior-exists rule, the no-prior→TimedOut rule, the Permanent immediate-degrade-no-carry rule, and the absent-normalized-as-Transient rule, often in near-identical prose/structure. The one notable gap is B2 omitting the transport-Err boundary contract that B1 and B3 both cover in detail.

Overall call: BD-DRIFT because the single most material gap — the spec's literal 'degrade after the window elapses' promise vs. the code's actual 'degrade only if there was never a prior mark, else carry forever and never degrade' behavior — is surfaced independently and consistently by both directions. Additional B-only-drift items (the Permanent/terminal category; the transport-Err boundary) ride alongside this as secondary, code-side-only surplus rather than changing the overall bidirectional classification.
